scope: Five exact identities from manufacturer-discovery-v1 with independently authored, native-executable reduced approximations.
limitations: These are part-specific engineering approximations derived from selected official data-sheet values. They are not vendor models, not manufacturer-qualified, not production-qualified, and do not turn the other discovery rows into executable models.

source.document: LM158, LM158A, LM258, LM258A, LM2904, LM2904V, LM358, LM358A Industry-Standard Dual Operational Amplifiers

derivation: Each channel uses A0/(1+s*A0/(2*pi*GBW)) followed by the stated output resistance.
The dominant capacitance is A0/(2*pi*GBW*Rdom); the two channels are independent except for shared supply pins.
Static diode clamps are offset so their nominal forward drop places the light-load output near the selected data-sheet rail headrooms.

validity.operating_conditions: Reduced small-signal voltage-amplifier use at 25 C, supply difference 5 V to 30 V, common-mode within the data-sheet range, and light external loading.
limitations: Full dual 8-pin context is retained, but package ordering suffixes are not distinguished.
No slew-rate limiting, input offset/bias/noise, common-mode failure, supply current, output-current limit, overload recovery, temperature dependence, distortion, or channel coupling.
The diode rail clamps are numerical approximations and do not reproduce load-dependent output swing; operation at either clamp is qualitative only.
The native static-diode path does not provide small-signal AC linearization for this nonlinear macro.

source.document: AD620 Low Cost, Low Power Instrumentation Amplifier

derivation: A native voltage-controlled source places VIN+ - VIN- across RG1/RG2; a current-controlled voltage source multiplies the resulting external RG current by 49.4 kohm.
Adding the direct differential term gives VOUT - VREF = (1 + 49.4 kohm/RG)*(VIN+ - VIN-) in DC.
A single RC pole uses the G=1 one-megahertz data-sheet bandwidth; it is not a gain-dependent AD620 frequency model.

validity.operating_conditions: DC gain formula for finite positive RG or open RG, 25 C, plus G=1 small-signal transient screening with supplies in the data-sheet operating range.
limitations: All eight package pins are retained; open RG requires distinct unconnected RG1 and RG2 nets, not both pins shorted to one node.
No gain error, offset, bias current, noise, CMRR/PSRR, input common-mode envelope, reference input loading, supply current, output-current limit, slew, settling, temperature, or distortion.
The one-megahertz pole is only the G=1 value; G=10, 100, and 1000 bandwidths are not modeled.
The rail clamps are qualitative outside light-load operation, and nonlinear AC analysis is not claimed.

source.document: MMBT3904L, SMMBT3904L General Purpose Transistors NPN Silicon
source.revision: MMBT3904LT1/D, current official repository copy reviewed

derivation: BF is the specified minimum 100 at IC=10 mA and VCE=1 V; reverse beta is an explicit unsourced numerical assumption.
IS is chosen so the forward-active Shockley term reaches 10 mA at the 0.85 V maximum saturated VBE; that conservative proxy is not a direct forward-active data-sheet fit.
CBE and CBC use the 8 pF and 4 pF maxima; TF is rounded from 1/(2*pi*300 MHz) after recognizing the capacitance contribution is operating-point dependent.

validity.operating_conditions: 25 C screening near the 10 mA characterization point, forward-active NPN operation, and voltages safely below published limits.
limitations: Ebers-Moll approximation only: no Early effect, high injection, avalanche, self-heating, temperature sweep, package parasitics, statistical spread, or reliable saturation/storage-time prediction.
IS and reverse beta are approximation choices, not manufacturer model parameters; the VBE source datum is a saturated-device maximum.
Constant capacitances use data-sheet maxima at their stated bias conditions and are not voltage dependent.

derivation: VTO is the explicit midpoint assumption of the 1.0 V to 2.5 V threshold range; it is not a typical value.
For the Level-1 saturation law ID=KP*(VGS-VTO)^2/2, KP=gfs^2/(2*ID)=0.016 A/V^2 from the 80 mS minimum at 200 mA.
CGD=Crss=5 pF, CGS=Ciss-Crss=45 pF, and CDS=Coss-Crss=20 pF use published maxima; the body-diode IS is chosen to reach 115 mA at 1.5 V with N=2.

validity.operating_conditions: 25 C, source-tied bulk, first-quadrant screening around the 200 mA transconductance condition, with voltages and power below published limits.
limitations: Level-1 square-law approximation only; it does not reproduce RDS(on), subthreshold, mobility degradation, velocity saturation, leakage, avalanche, temperature, self-heating, SOA, or switching charge.
Threshold midpoint, zero channel-length modulation, and body-diode emission coefficient are explicit modeling assumptions, not manufacturer typical values.
Constant capacitances combine maxima specified at one bias and therefore are deliberately conservative but not a charge-conserving nonlinear capacitance model.

fields: maximum forward voltage at 1 mA and 10 mA

derivation: At 300.15 K, solving I=IS*exp(V/(N*VT)) through the two published maximum points (1 mA, 0.715 V) and (10 mA, 0.855 V) gives N=2.3507211259 and IS=7.8137073765 nA.
The native static Shockley primitive omits the minus-one term only negligibly at those forward currents; tests use the exact native expm1 convention.
The fit is an upper-limit curve through two guaranteed maxima, not a typical measured I-V curve or a conservative bound between/away from those points.

validity.operating_conditions: 25 C static forward-conduction screening from approximately 1 mA to 10 mA, below published voltage, current, and power limits.
limitations: No series resistance, reverse leakage law, breakdown, temperature dependence, self-heating, junction capacitance, forward recovery, reverse recovery, package parasitics, or statistical spread.
The data-sheet forward-voltage values are maxima, not typical samples; this two-point curve is not manufacturer qualification or validation.
The 1.5 pF and 4 ns limits are retained as evidence only because the native static diode card cannot represent them.
